description: Request dispatcher whose opcode table registers handlers through token pasting (HANDLER(rev) -> h_rev) defined in another file

bugs.trigger: proto_reply (or the last request of proto_run): opcode byte 0x04 followed by 1..64 payload bytes; h_rev reads p[n - i] with i = 0, one byte past the payload

lexer_expected: The lexer sees no reference from src/dispatch.c to h_* (the names exist only after h_##name pasting in the static ops[] table), so module 'dispatch' has required_sources [src/dispatch.c] and its harness fails to link (undefined h_ping, h_echo, h_sum, h_rev, h_upper; verified): S02-1 is missed through the real API. It offers the five handlers as entry points of module 'handlers'. They take an internal struct reply * (not an API shape), so a direct harness either cannot build them or must invent the reply buffer; a NULL or wrongly sized buf crashes any handler (false positives), and only a correctly sized one could reach S02-1 by accident.

trust.rule: step I7, no threat model: a library alone, so its API is untrusted (default, boundary) and every other function trusted (default)
